scenes.name: Spanish boogie / spaghetti y megamix
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: La disco llega con la Transición y el Destape (Susana Estrada); Barrabás triunfa en Europa. La distribuidora Blanco y Negro trae el italodisco («spaguetti») y el tecno-pop a las discotecas de Levante; de ahí una generación de DJs virtuosos (Raúl Orellana, Toni Peret, José María Castells) y el megamix (Bolero Mix, Max Mix). Debajo del pop de glamour (Tino Casal, Miguel Bosé, Iván), un boogie electropop subterráneo que el DJ Kigo rescató como «Espanish Boogie».

podcast.title: Member of The Dream Team
podcast.body: José María Castells formed "The Dream Team" with Quique Tejada and Tony Peret at Max Music. This group was responsible for producing almost all of the company's megamixes, achieving star status in Spain and providing the soundtrack for parties, road trips, and summers for an entire generation. "Junta Toni Peret, hijo de María Castéis, formaron el Dream Team, quienes pasaron a realizar prácticamente todos los Megamixes de la compañía."

podcast.title: New Mixer for Max Music
podcast.body: José María Castells, a young local DJ, was recruited by Max Music alongside Tony Peret to replace Mike Platinas and Javier Usia. They became the official Megamixers for the label following the success and innovation of Max Mix 3. "En Max Music no perdieron el tiempo, y encontraron los institutos perfectos de Mike Platinas y Javier Usia en Tony Peretta y José María Castéis, unos jóvenes digis locales."

podcast.title: Victim of Mistaken Identity Kidnapping
podcast.body: On September 3, 1998, José María Castells was mistakenly kidnapped by 13 Mexican hitmen hired by Miguel DeGa, who intended to abduct Ricardo Campoy. Castells was targeted because he drove the same car model as Campoy. He was gagged and beaten but managed to escape his captors during a lapse in their vigilance, reaching a police station in Berga. "Los matones se confundieron y secuestraron la José María Castig, quien llevaba el mismo modelo de coche que Campoy."
